title: Combining Parameterized Pulses and Contextual Subspace for More Practical VQE
problem: Traditional CNOT-based quantum circuits limit access to certain Hilbert space regions, and computing complete Hamiltonians via VQE requires many qubits and measurements. Scaling VQE to simulate larger molecular systems is impractical with current approaches.
motivation: Reducing quantum resource requirements makes VQE viable for simulating larger molecular structures on near-term quantum devices.
method: SpacePulse combines parameterized quantum pulses—adjustable quantum operations that can explore regions of the quantum state space unreachable with traditional gates—with the contextual subspace method, which computes corrections using only a subset of qubits and measurements rather than simulating the full system. This combination enables flexible quantum operations beyond gate-based decomposition. A Pauli grouping strategy (organizing measurements by grouping related quantum properties) optimizes measurement efficiency.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining parameterized quantum pulses (adjustable quantum operations) with the contextual subspace method (computing corrections using only a subset of qubits and measurements) to dramatically reduce quantum resource requirements while maintaining solution accuracy.
contributions: SpacePulse framework integrating parameterized pulses and contextual subspace methods
Demonstrated reduction in required qubits and measurements compared to traditional VQE
Pauli grouping strategy for optimizing measurement overhead
Enhanced scalability for molecular structure simulation with reduced quantum resources
